subject: Egress gateway IP binding + firewall constraints for Redwood private endpoint
messages:
From: NetworkOps <netops@veridian.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Egress gateway IP binding and firewall constraints for Redwood private endpoint

Hi Vivek / Monica,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of Acme Health's security review for the private deployment we need a formalized list of outbound IPs (for NAT or egress gateway binding) plus a recommended minimal set of firewall rules for the private endpoint. Our security team also asked for behavior when the dedicated pool is degraded (fallback to hosted endpoints) — specifically which hostnames/IPs will be used and whether TLS certs are customer-authorized.

Could you provide: 1) canonical list of IPs your egress gateway will originate from (and an update cadence), 2) required outbound ports/protocols and FQDNs (for both normal and fallback), 3) any recommendations for NAT timeouts or connection tracking settings for long-running streaming calls, 4) a one-page attachment template we can drop into our firewall change request.

Appreciate quick turnaround; the change window is scheduled for 2026-09-10.

--
Network Operations
Veridian (partner managing Acme edge infra)
attachments: none

---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: NetworkOps <netops@veridian.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Egress gateway IP binding and firewall constraints for Redwood private endpoint

Hi Tom / NetworkOps team,

Thanks — attached is the current set of egress IP blocks we can commit to for the next quarter (redwood-egress-ipblocks.csv). Key points:

- IP binding: We can guarantee a set of up to 6 public IPv4 addresses per region for outbound connections from the private endpoint. The attached CSV lists the current addresses for the US region. We rotate/update these quarterly; we'll give 7 days' notice for changes.
- Ports/FQDNs: Minimum outbound: TCP/443 to the following hostnames: api.redwood-inference.com, auth.redwood-inference.com, metrics.redwood-inference.com. Additionally, TCP/443 to model variant CDNs (model-*.redwoodcdn.com). DNS (UDP/TCP/53) must be allowed to your internal resolvers. We also use outbound TCP/443 to s3-compatible artifact storage endpoints in the same region for model pulls.
- Streaming/NAT: For long-lived streaming (websocket/long-poll), set NAT connection tracking timeout to >= 30m idle; recommend 60m to be safe. Connection reuse is critical — avoid aggressive connection tear-down.
- Fallback behavior: If Dedicated capacity is unavailable, traffic will be routed to our hosted control plane for inference. Fallback uses the same TLS certificates presented by our gateway; customer traffic is still over TLS terminated at Redwood's gateways. For stricter security customers who require mTLS to a customer-managed endpoint, we provide an optional TLS client cert option — let us know if you want that enabled.
- Firewall template: attached egress-firewall-template.yml (simple firewall rules + justification comments).

I've attached two files: redwood-egress-ipblocks.csv and egress-firewall-template.yml.

Next steps: let us know whether Acme will bind those 6 IP addresses on the edge NAT, and confirm if you need the IPs as single addresses or CIDR blocks.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Deployments — Redwood Inference
---

From: Acme IT Security <it-security@acmehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, NetworkOps <netops@veridian.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Egress gateway IP binding and firewall constraints for Redwood private endpoint

Vivek / team,

Partial ack — thanks for the quick response. A few clarifying items from our side:

1) We need both the final IPs as single A addresses and as the minimal enclosing CIDRs for our internal ticketing. The CSV is fine but please add a top-line row with the CIDRs.
2) For the fallback to hosted, we require explicit hostnames (not only IPs) so our TLS inspection policy can whitelist SNI. Could you provide the full list of hostnames used in fallback (including any telemetry/metrics endpoints)?
3) We must see a signed statement that Redwood will not initiate inbound connections to our VPC (no reverse shells :) ) — just outbound only. Can you sign and return; a short PDF attestation is sufficient.

Also: We operate a strict egress proxy that terminates TLS for inspection. Can you confirm that your TLS certificate Common Names will be stable for the quarter (no wildcard rotation that would break SNI allowlist)?

Regards,
Sara Ling
Acme Health — IT Security

---

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Acme IT Security <it-security@acmehealth.com>, NetworkOps <netops@veridian.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Egress gateway IP binding and firewall constraints for Redwood private endpoint

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks — quick clarifications from product/security side:

- We'll produce an updated CSV with the CIDR summary row by EOD today.
- Full fallback hostnames (for SNI allowlisting): api.redwood-inference.com, hosted-fallback.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.com, auth.redwood-inference.com, models.redwood-inference.com. We will not use ephemeral hostnames during fallback — these are stable hostnames and we guarantee no sudden CN/name changes inside the quarter.
- TLS certs: primary gateway uses certs issued by DigiCert (CN=*.redwood-inference.com) for the session. If you require stricter SNI-based policy, we can provide the specific SAN list used by the gateway. For customers with TLS inspection proxies, we recommend either allowing the SNI or configuring the proxy to trust our root for inspection.
- Attestation: Attached signed-egress-ack.pdf; confirms only outbound connections originate from Redwood to customer VPCs, no inbound connection attempts nor active probing.
- Operational recommendation: Configure health-check ports on the firewall to allow quick connectivity tests from our maintenance IPs and set any upstream proxy to allow 60m idle for streaming.

If this matches your requirements we can schedule the change window for 2026-09-10 and I'll mark the ticket green.

Best,
Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: signed-egress-ack.pdf

---

From: NetworkOps <netops@veridian.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Acme IT Security <it-security@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Egress gateway IP binding and firewall constraints for Redwood private endpoint

Thanks everyone — we have everything we need to open the change request. Confirmed: 6 IPs (as individual addresses + CIDR summary), SNI list for fallback, signed attestation received. We will apply the firewall rules per the YAML template and set NAT idle timeout to 60m.

I'll follow up with the change request ticket ID once it's created.

Tom Reynolds
NetworkOps — Veridian
attachments: none
